excerpt: Vaccitech, the Oxford spinout behind early work on the Oxford/AstraZeneca vaccine, became Barinthus Biotherapeutics in 2023 and agreed to merge with Clywedog in 2025.
content:
Vaccitech was a biotechnology company spun out of the University of Oxford's Jenner Institute in 2016. Its early work included the co-invention and early development of the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, Vaxzevria. The company later listed on Nasdaq.

On 6 November 2023 Vaccitech announced that it had changed its name to Barinthus Biotherapeutics, trading under the ticker BRNS from 7 November. The company said the old name suggested a purely vaccine-focused business, while its work had moved to T-cell immunotherapies for infectious diseases, autoimmunity and cancer. The new name comes from a figure in the Arthurian legends described as a guide and navigator. The old vaccitech.co.uk address now redirects to barinthusbio.com.

In 2026 the company's lead programme is VTP-1000, an experimental treatment for coeliac disease. Barinthus said enrolment in the Phase 1 AVALON trial was complete with 42 subjects, and that topline data from its multiple-ascending-dose part were expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. For the second quarter of 2026 it reported a net loss of $10.6 million and cash of $59.6 million at 30 June.

On 30 September 2025 Barinthus and Clywedog Therapeutics announced an all-stock merger. Under the original terms, Barinthus shareholders would own about 34% of the combined company and Clywedog's about 66%; the combined business would be renamed Clywedog Therapeutics and trade on Nasdaq as CLYD. The merger agreement was amended in February 2026, and the company's later filings still describe the deal as pending. We have not seen confirmation that it has closed.

This is a drug developer, not a product you can buy. It appears on 100xFounder as part of our coverage of startups and their outcomes.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

faq.a: It renamed itself Barinthus Biotherapeutics in November 2023 and now trades on Nasdaq as BRNS.

faq.q: Did Vaccitech make the Oxford COVID vaccine?
faq.a: It co-invented and did early development work on the Oxford/AstraZeneca vaccine, Vaxzevria, which AstraZeneca developed and sold.

faq.q: Is Barinthus merging with another company?
faq.a: Yes. In September 2025 it agreed an all-stock merger with Clywedog Therapeutics; the combined company is to be called Clywedog Therapeutics. The deal was still pending in the company's latest filings we saw.
